commit.message:
LU-20099 nrs: reserved rate combined with weight for mClock

The weight patch adds the reserve plus weight dimension set. A
policy of that set guarantees a floor for each class and shares the
surplus by weight. The dequeue path takes the reserved tree first,
and it falls through to the weight tree. See nrs_mclock_req_get().

An off limit dimension means an unlimited limit. A start command of
"mclock projid reserve=1 weight=1" therefore starts a policy with no
ceiling. That policy keeps a floor and a weight share.

The scheduler also accepts the limit plus weight set. Such a policy
has no reserve tree. The mClock model reads a zero reservation as no
floor, and dmClock gives the same meaning.

The rule dump now reports the weight of a rule, so an administrator
can read back the configuration.

The patch reworks sanityn/test_77vh. The scenarios share one
implementation. The skip checks move into nrs_server_backlog_prep(),
so the version gate runs before the helper changes a parameter.
